title: Compatible coefficient encodings and sheaf-level origin
statement: Use the module sites and exchange maps of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Let B be a finite discrete commutative ring killed by the prime ell, k a field of positive prime characteristic different from ell, and sq any commutative square of separated finite-type k-schemes. Given a family of monoidal identifications of its pulled-back condensed coefficient rings with the sheafified constant rings on all schemes and the constant-ring internal-module encoding hypothesis, there exist abelian coefficient equivalences E0 on X and E1 on Y-prime such that every constructible internal sheaf on X has etale sheaf origin under comparison inverse image followed by E0. Their concretely derived realization functors identify the four vertices and each of the three unit-square-counit arrows of exchange, on every bounded constructible realized complex. These are sheaf-origin and stepwise coherence assertions; no arbitrary bounded-complex origin or assembled arrow comparison is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.2, Lemmas 5.4.1 and 5.4.3; Stacks Project Tag 09AK

proof.text: Construct the same sectionwise equivalence on every scheme from the proved pointwise internal-module equivalence and a single monoidal ring identification at the profinite point.

Transport internal constructibility under this explicit encoding, apply the existing ordinary finite-ring pro-etale constructible origin theorem, and map the resulting isomorphism through E followed by its counit.

Take coherent pullback comparisons and invertible canonical right mates. Mathlib mate identities construct their unit and counit equations. The explicit categorical three-step theorem constructs all four vertex isomorphisms and all three commuting squares. Apply the separate general formal transport theorem to identify the specified restricted factors and append their defining factorizations.

theorem finiteDiscreteExchange_coefficientRealization [DiscreteTopology B] [Finite B]
    (hB : (ℓ : B) = 0) (sq : CommSq g' f' f g)
    (eR : ∀ T : Scheme.{u},
      Sheaf.sheafifyRingPresheaf.{u + 1, u, u + 1} (Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
        ((Functor.const T.ProEtᵒᵖ).obj (RingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} B))) ≅
          condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} B) T)
    (heR : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}, IsMonHom (eR T).hom)
    (hEncoding : ∀ T : Scheme.{u},
      ∃ G : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) Ab.{u + 1})
          (Sheaf.sheafifyRingPresheaf.{u + 1, u, u + 1} (Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
            ((Functor.const T.ProEtᵒᵖ).obj
              (RingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} B) : RingCat.{u + 1}))) ⥤
            Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B)),
        G.IsEquivalence ∧ Nonempty (G ⋙
          sheafCompose (Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
            (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B)) Ab.{u + 1}) ≅
          Mod.forget (D := Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) Ab.{u + 1})
            (Sheaf.sheafifyRingPresheaf.{u + 1, u, u + 1} (Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
              ((Functor.const T.ProEtᵒᵖ).obj
              (RingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} B) : RingCat.{u + 1}))))) :
    haveI : IsFinitenessCoefficient ℓ (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} B) :=
      .torsion B 1 (by rw [pow_one]; exact hB)
    ∃ (E0 : FiniteDiscreteProEtaleSheaves B X ≌ FiniteDiscreteInternalModules B X)
      (E1 : FiniteDiscreteProEtaleSheaves B Y' ≌ FiniteDiscreteInternalModules B Y'),
      (∀ M : FiniteDiscreteInternalModules B X,
        ProEtale.IsConstructibleModuleObject
          (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} B) X) M →
        (ν^*(X)[ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B)] ⋙ E0.functor).essImage M) ∧
      finiteDiscreteExchangeSteps B ℓ k sq
        (finiteDiscreteRealization B X E0) (finiteDiscreteRealization B Y' E1)
